text: Blurred vision: Blurred vision is an ocular symptom where vision becomes less precise and there is added difficulty to resolve fine details.

Diplopia: Diplopia is the simultaneous perception of two images of a single object that may be displaced in relation to each other. Also called double vision, it is a loss of visual focus under regular conditions, and is often voluntary.

Dry eyes: Dry eye disease (DED), also known as keratoconjunctivitis sicca, is the condition of having dry eyes. The term dry eye syndrome was formerly used, but is now avoided following advances that have established it as a distinct disease entity.
Eye itching: A presenting complaint characterised by eye itching.

Eye pain: Eye pain, also called ophthomalgia or ocular pain, is a nonspecific term for pain in one or both eyes, around the eyes, or behind the eyes. It may encompass minor eye irritation, aching, or burning sensation to intense and prolonged pain.
Eye swelling: A presenting complaint characterised by eye swelling.

Glare: Glare is a fiber metal laminate (FML) composed of several very thin layers of metal interspersed with layers of S-2 glass-fiber pre-preg, bonded together with a matrix such as epoxy. The uni-directional pre-preg layers may be aligned in different directions to suit predicted stress conditions.

Photophobia: Photophobia is a medical symptom of abnormal intolerance to visual perception of light. As a medical symptom, photophobia is not a morbid fear or phobia, but an experience of discomfort or pain to the eyes due to light exposure or by presence of actual physical sensitivity of the eyes, though the term is sometimes additionally applied to abnormal or irrational fear of light, such as heliophobia.
Photopsia: Photopsia is the presence of perceived flashes of light in the field of vision.
Red eye: Red eye, red-eye, redeye or variants may refer to:.

Vision loss: Visual or vision impairment is the partial or total inability of visual perception. In the absence of treatment such as corrective eyewear, assistive devices, and medical treatment, visual impairment may cause the individual difficulties with normal daily tasks, including reading and walking.

Visual distortion: A hallucination is a perception in the absence of an external context stimulus that has the compelling sense of reality. They are distinguishable from several related phenomena, such as dreaming, which does not involve wakefulness; pseudohallucination, which does not mimic real perception, and is accurately perceived as unreal; illusion, which involves distorted or misinterpreted real perception; and mental imagery, which does not mimic real perception, and is under voluntary control.

Watery eyes: Tears are a transparent fluid secreted primarily by the lacrimal glands found in the eyes of all land mammals. According to the mode of production, tears are classified into four types: basal, closed eye, emotional, and reflex.

Acute angle-closure glaucoma, bilateral: Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that can lead to damage of the optic nerve, which transmits visual information from the eye to the brain. Glaucoma may cause vision loss if left untreated. Common presenting complaints: Red Eye, Eye Pain, Photophobia. Associated symptoms: Eye Pain, Halos Around Lights, Blurred Vision, Nausea And Vomiting, Mid Dilated Non Reactive Pupil. Risk factors: Increased Pressure In The Eye, Family History, High Blood Pressure. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Risk factors: Contact Lens Wear, Adenovirus Exposure, Ocular Surface Disease, Immunosuppression. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Cystoid macular edema following cataract surgery, bilateral: Macular edema occurs when fluid and protein deposits collect on or under the macula of the eye and causes it to thicken and swell (edema). The swelling may distort a person's central vision, because the macula holds tightly packed cones that provide sharp, clear, central vision to enable a person to see detail, form, and color that is directly in the centre of the field of view. Common presenting complaints: Visual Distortion. Associated symptoms: Decreased Central Vision, Metamorphopsia, Cystic Spaces On Oct. Risk factors: Diabetes, Uveitis, Pseudoexfoliation, Retinal Disease. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Glare sensitivity: Glare sensitivity is a visual disturbance characterized by discomfort and impaired vision when exposed to bright light. Common presenting complaints: Glare. Associated symptoms: Photophobia, Eye Strain, Headache, Blurred Vision. Risk factors: Dry Eye, Cataracts, Refractive Errors, Migraine. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Associated symptoms: Arteriolar Narrowing, Arteriovenous Nicking, Flame Shaped Hemorrhages, Cotton Wool Spots, Papilledema. Risk factors: Hypertension, Diabetes, Smoking, Ckd. Age relevance: . Meibomian gland dysfunction right upper eyelid: Meibomian gland dysfunction of the right upper eyelid is a chronic disorder characterized by obstruction of the meibomian glands leading to altered tear film and ocular surface irritation. Common presenting complaints: Watery Eyes. Associated symptoms: Dry Eye Symptoms, Gritty Or Foreign Body Sensation, Eyelid Margin Telangiectasia, Crusting Of Lashes. Risk factors: Age, Hormonal Changes, Contact Lens Wear, Blepharitis. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

The pain often affects one side of the head, but can affect both. Common presenting complaints: Photophobia, Photopsia, Blurred Vision, Visual Distortion. Associated symptoms: Headache, Vomiting, Nausea, Burping, Photophobia. Risk factors: Environmental And Genetic. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Multiple sclerosis, unspecified: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic and neurodegenerative autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks myelin, the insulating cover of nerve cells, causing damage to the central nervous system. This impairs the nervous system's ability to transmit signals. Common presenting complaints: Diplopia. Associated symptoms: Chronic Neuropathic Pain. Risk factors: Unknown. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Neonatal conjunctivitis and dacryocystitis: Neonatal conjunctivitis and dacryocystitis are acute bacterial infections of the eye and lacrimal sac occurring within the first month of life. Common presenting complaints: Eye Swelling. Associated symptoms: Purulent Conjunctival Discharge, Chemosis, Preauricular Swelling, Corneal Ulceration. Risk factors: Maternal Genital Infection, Prematurity, Low Birth Weight, Prolonged Rupture Of Membranes. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Common presenting complaints: Watery Eyes, Eye Swelling, Eye Itching. Associated symptoms: Itching Of The Eye, Tearing Epiphora, Redness Conjunctival Hyperemia, Follicular Reaction On Conjunctiva, Photophobia. Risk factors: Atopy, Pollenexposure, Dustmiteexposure. Other giant cell arteritis: Giant cell arteritis (GCA), also called temporal arteritis, is an inflammatory autoimmune disease of large blood vessels. It is the most common type of systemic vasculitis affecting adults. Common presenting complaints: Photophobia. Associated symptoms: Headache, Fatigue, Fever, Weight Loss, Diplopia, Tenderness, Jaw Pain. Risk factors: Age>50, Female Sex, White Ethnicity, Hla Drb1*04. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Other non-diabetic proliferative retinopathy, bilateral: A bilateral retinal condition characterized by neovascularization in the absence of diabetes, leading to potential vision loss. Common presenting complaints: Glare, Photopsia, Blurred Vision, Vision Loss. Associated symptoms: Often Asymptomatic, But Can Cause Spots In The Eye And Vision Loss. Risk factors: Long Term Poor Control Of Diabetes Mellitus. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Other optic neuritis: Optic neuritis (ON) is a debilitating condition that is defined as inflammation of cranial nerve II which results in disruption of the neurologic pathways that allow visual sensory information received by the retina to be able to be transmitted to the visual cortex of the brain. This disorder of the optic nerve may arise through various pathophysiologic mechanisms, such as through demyelination or inflammation, leading to partial or total loss of vision. Common presenting complaints: Glare, Blurred Vision, Vision Loss, Visual Distortion. Associated symptoms: Loss Of Vision, Loss Of Colour Vision, Pain Worsening On Eye Movements. Risk factors: Autoimmune, Infection, Vaccination, Medication. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Common presenting complaints: Vision Loss. Associated symptoms: Visual Field Loss, Optic Disc Cupping, Elevated Intraocular Pressure, Color Vision Changes. Risk factors: Increased Pressure In The Eye, Family History, High Blood Pressure. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Retinal detachment with retinal dialysis, bilateral: Retinal detachment is a condition where the retina pulls away from the tissue underneath it. It may start in a small area, but without quick treatment, it can spread across the entire retina, leading to serious vision loss and possibly blindness. Common presenting complaints: Photopsia, Visual Distortion. Associated symptoms: Photopsia, Floaters, Visual Field Loss, Retinal Dialysis. Risk factors: High Myopia, Trauma, Lattice Degeneration, Cataract Surgery. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

The disease usually begins in the lungs, skin, or lymph nodes. Common presenting complaints: Dry Eyes. Associated symptoms: Cough, Dyspnea. Risk factors: Unknown. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Sympathetic uveitis, unspecified eye: In ophthalmology, sympathetic ophthalmia (SO), also called spared eye injury, is a granulomatous diffuse inflammation of the uveal layer (uveitis) of both eyes following trauma to one eye. It can leave the affected person completely blind. Common presenting complaints: Red Eye. Associated symptoms: Floaters, Photophobia. Risk factors: Ocular Trauma, Ocular Surgery, Intraocular Inflammation, Systemic Inflammatory Disease. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Transient neonatal myasthenia gravis: Transient neonatal myasthenia gravis, i.e., TNMG, and its more severe form, fetal acetylcholine receptor inactivation syndrome, is one of the various types of myasthenia gravis. MG is an autoimmune disease in which individuals form antibodies that circulate in their blood, enter tissues, bind to certain proteins in the neuromuscular junctions of skeletal muscles, and thereby reduce the number or ability of these skeletal muscles to contract when appropriately stimulated by acetylcholine. Common presenting complaints: Diplopia. Associated symptoms: Varying Degrees Muscle Weakness, Double Vision, Drooping Eyelids, Trouble Talking, Trouble Walking. Risk factors: Autoimmune Disease. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .
